stories.title: Industrial production down by 0.5% in the euro area and by 0.3% in the EU
stories.description: Overview In August 2026, compared with July 2026, seasonally adjusted industrial production decreased by 0.5% in the euro area and by 0.3% in the EU, according to first estimates from Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union. In July 2026, industrial production fell by 0.3% in the euro area and by 0.4% in the EU. In August 2026, compared with August 2025, industrial production decreased by 1.1% in the euro area and by 0.2% in the EU. Monthly comparison by main industrial grouping and by Member State In the euro area in August 2026, compared with July 2026, industrial production decreased for intermediate goods by 0.8%, decreased for energy by 0.6%, increased for capital goods by 0.4%, increased for durable consumer goods by 0.2%, decreased for non-durable consumer goods by 2.7%. In the EU, industrial production decreased for intermediate goods by 0.3%, decreased for energy by 0.5%, increased for capital goods by 0.7%, remained stable for durable consumer goods, decreased for non-durable consumer goods by 2.3%. The largest monthly decreases were recorded in Belgium (-5.1%), Ireland (-3.1%) and Portugal (-2.0%). The highest increases were observed in Sweden (+6.5%), Estonia (+4.3%) and the Netherlands (+2.6%). Annual comparison by main industrial grouping and by Member State In the euro area in August 2026, compared with August 2025, industrial production decreased for intermediate goods by 0.4%, increased for energy by 3.1%, increased for capital goods by 3.0%, increased for durable consumer goods by 0.4%, decreased for non-durable consumer goods by 9.1%. In the EU, industrial production increased for intermediate goods by 0.3%, increased for energy by 2.4%, increased for capital goods by 3.6%, increased for durable consumer goods by 0.8%, decreased for non-durable consumer goods by 6.7%. The largest annual decreases were recorded in Ireland (-15.0%), Belgium (-7.1%) and Bulgaria (-5.4%). The highest increases were observed in the Netherlands (+9.8%), Hungary (+8.8%) and Denmark (+8.3%). stories.title: Warming-driven lower-tropospheric stratification intensifies ducting over global oceans
stories.description: Under global warming, the marine atmospheric boundary layer shows an increase in lower-tropospheric stratification. These thermodynamic shifts alter vertical refractivity gradients and can modulate atmospheric ducts, which are natural waveguides crucial for beyond-line-of-sight electromagnetic propagation. Using ERA5 reanalysis data from 1940 to 2025, we find a global-scale intensification of atmospheric ducts over oceans at mid- to low-latitude, with a robust increasing trend in atmospheric duct occurrence probability, strength and top height. Mechanistically, this intensification is intrinsically coupled with the sustained increase in static stability in the marine atmospheric boundary layer. Although interannual climate modes, such as the El Niño/Southern Oscillation, modulate these anomalies, the long-term warming trend dominates the long-term trend. Ultimately, continuous warming is shifting the marine atmospheric background state towards a highly stratified regime favouring more frequent and intense ducting, with implications for global maritime communication, radar and navigation systems. Atmospheric ducts are waveguides that affect electromagnetic propagation in the atmosphere, affecting radar and other technologies. Here the authors show that warming intensifies such ducting over mid- to low-latitude oceans.
